project: The Sound Above: UGtastic Oral History Rewatch Series

episodes.title: The First Room: Chicago Alt.NET & Escaping Corporate Monoliths
episodes.sound_above_inquiry: Who inspired the engineers breaking free from enterprise Microsoft silos? How did grassroots peer groups form before commercial developer platforms existed?
episodes.chicago_context: Chicago Alt.NET was the precursor room for dozens of Chicago developers who later founded startups, consultancy practices, and user groups.
episodes.ai_era_parallel: Just as Alt.NET questioned monolithic enterprise frameworks, modern engineers must question monolithic cloud AI abstractions and reclaim local control.

episodes.title: The Ambassador: ChicagoRuby & Grassroots Hospitality
episodes.sound_above_inquiry: Who showed the early community organizers how to welcome newcomers with radical hospitality? What made ChicagoRuby a durable institution for two decades?
episodes.chicago_context: Ray Hightower served as the welcoming ambassador bridging corporate IT, independent consultants, and open-source practitioners.
episodes.ai_era_parallel: In an era of automated code synthesis, human hospitality and community mentorship become more valuable, not less.

episodes.title: Pair Friday in Libertyville: Apprenticeship & Terminal Workbenches
episodes.sound_above_inquiry: Who taught the 8th Light founders the discipline of apprenticeship? How did Carl Sagan and cosmic perspective shape their company philosophy?
episodes.chicago_context: 8th Light was founded in the Chicago suburbs, pioneering paid resident apprenticeships long before bootcamp pipelines existed.
episodes.ai_era_parallel: Pair programming with an AI agent requires the exact same discipline as pairing with a junior apprentice: legible contracts, small steps, and continuous review.

episodes.title: The Apprenticeship Move: From Psychology to Craftsmanship
episodes.sound_above_inquiry: Who inspired Dave Hoover and Adewale Oshineye to write Apprenticeship Patterns? What can senior engineers learn from psychological mentorship models?
episodes.chicago_context: Dave Hoover helped lead Obtiva in Chicago, creating one of the earliest structured consultancy apprenticeship programs.
episodes.ai_era_parallel: Apprenticeship Patterns ('Expose Your Ignorance', 'Deep Roots', 'Record What You Learn') are the antidote to shallow LLM copy-paste culture.

episodes.title: The 17-Year Continuous Room: Founding SCMC & Suburban Craftsmanship
episodes.sound_above_inquiry: What sustained a monthly practitioner meetup in McHenry County for seventeen straight years without corporate sponsorship or speaker fees?
episodes.chicago_context: Mike Hall, Jim Suchy, and Ryan Gerry founded SCMC in spring 2009 following Manifesto Signatory #106, hosted at Follett and Panera Bread.
episodes.ai_era_parallel: Grassroots community rooms provide psychological safety to test ideas, fail safely, and evaluate AI tooling with skeptical peer review.

episodes.title: Cranking Design to 11: Deliberate Practice & The Four Rules
episodes.sound_above_inquiry: Who taught Corey Haines to look at code through the lens of deliberate musical practice? What was the origin of Global Day of Coderetreat?
episodes.chicago_context: Corey was a central figure in the Chicago craftsmanship circuit, holding early retreats at Obtiva and 8th Light offices.
episodes.ai_era_parallel: Kent Beck's Four Rules of Simple Design become the primary evaluation rubric for code generated by AI models.
episodes.companion_video: Understanding the 4 Rules of Simple Design (Corey Haines)

episodes.title: The Toolmakers: Watir, WatiN & Automating the Browser
episodes.sound_above_inquiry: Who paved the way for automated acceptance testing before Selenium was mature? What was the open-source maintenance burden on early Rubyists?
episodes.chicago_context: TicketsNow in Crystal Lake was one of the early testbeds for WatiN and WatiR distributed inventory testing in 2006.
episodes.ai_era_parallel: Modern agentic browsers (Playwright, Puppeteer) follow the exact architectural lineage established by Watir twenty years ago.

episodes.title: Clean Code in the Wild: Daily Practice & Object Mentor Wisdom
episodes.sound_above_inquiry: Who mentored the Object Mentor consultants? How did Ward Cunningham's early WikiWikiWeb discussions influence their naming rules?
episodes.chicago_context: Object Mentor was headquartered in northern Illinois (Lake Zurich and Gurnee), directly anchoring the Chicago agile cluster.
episodes.ai_era_parallel: Readable, intention-revealing names matter even more when AI models write and parse millions of tokens across codebases.

episodes.title: Cross-Pollination: Game Jams, Functional Code & Alt.NET
episodes.sound_above_inquiry: What inspired game developers and functional programmers to bring their experimental energy into corporate craftsmanship meetups?
episodes.chicago_context: International speakers traveled to Chicago for SCNA, bringing European Alt.NET and functional programming perspectives.
episodes.ai_era_parallel: Video game architecture (entity-component systems, event loops) offers superior mental models for real-time AI agent orchestration.

episodes.title: The Fast Feedback Loop: Destroy All Software & Unix Workbenches
episodes.sound_above_inquiry: Who inspired Gary Bernhardt to push terminal speed, Vim efficiency, and sub-second test suites to absolute perfection?
episodes.chicago_context: Gary's SCNA talk on boundaries and his legendary lightning talks shook up the Chicago craftsmanship and Ruby scenes.
episodes.ai_era_parallel: If your test suite takes 10 minutes to run, autonomous agents cannot verify changes. Fast, isolated feedback is essential for agentic loops.

episodes.title: Software as Communication: BDD, Humility & Deliberate Discovery
episodes.sound_above_inquiry: Who inspired Dan North to challenge dogma? Why did he refuse to monetize or certify Behavior-Driven Development?
episodes.chicago_context: Dan North's keynote at SCNA 2013 reframed craftsmanship from rigid rules to human communication and business empathy.
episodes.ai_era_parallel: 'Deliberate discovery' assumes ignorance is our constraint. Modern AI prompts fail when they assume certainty; humility yields better architectures.

episodes.title: Unlearning Dogma: From Snowbird 2001 to Elixir & Modern Craft
episodes.sound_above_inquiry: What inspired the original Pragmatic Programmer when writing with Andy Hunt in 1999? What led him to challenge Agile commercialization?
episodes.chicago_context: PragDave delivered one of the most provocative keynotes at SCNA Chicago, challenging attendees not to turn craftsmanship into a cult.
episodes.ai_era_parallel: Rules that hardened twenty years ago must be re-evaluated. The spirit of the Pragmatic Programmer is experimentation, not orthodoxy.
episodes.companion_video: Dave Thomas: Agile is Dead (Long Live Agility)

episodes.title: The Truck Driver's Wisdom: Developer Humility & Tooling Craft
episodes.sound_above_inquiry: Who showed Hadi Hariri that software engineers are not special snowflakes? Why does empathy for real-world workers matter in systems design?
episodes.chicago_context: Hadi represented JetBrains at Chicago conferences, arguing for ergonomic IDEs that empower developers without arrogance.
episodes.ai_era_parallel: Software engineers must remember they are toolsmiths serving human needs, especially as AI generates the boilerplate.
episodes.companion_video: Hadi Hariri: Refactoring to Functional Style

episodes.title: The Sociological System: Pair Programming, DevChix & Team Cognition
episodes.sound_above_inquiry: Who inspired Sarah Mei to analyze software engineering through sociological and group dynamic frameworks rather than purely mechanical ones?
episodes.chicago_context: Sarah was a keynote voice at Chicago tech events, reshaping how the community thought about team structures and inclusive spaces.
episodes.ai_era_parallel: Multi-agent systems suffer from the exact same communication breakdown and cognitive overhead as human developer teams.

episodes.title: Practical Design: Small Methods, True Cost of Change & POODR
episodes.sound_above_inquiry: Who were the Smalltalk mentors who taught Sandi Metz message sending, duck typing, and radical simplicity in design?
episodes.chicago_context: Sandi's visits to Chicago events brought clarity to object-oriented design that cut through academic jargon.
episodes.ai_era_parallel: Small, single-responsibility methods with intention-revealing messages are the single easiest format for AI agents to reason about without hallucination.
episodes.companion_video: Sandi Metz: Magic Tricks of Testing (RailsConf 2013)

episodes.title: The Chicago Corridor: Software as Writing & The TDD Reckoning
episodes.sound_above_inquiry: Who inspired DHH's literary aesthetic of code? What was happening behind the scenes during the 'TDD is Dead' debates?
episodes.chicago_context: Recorded in a quiet hotel corridor during RailsConf 2014 in Chicago, right after the seismic 'TDD is Dead' keynote.
episodes.ai_era_parallel: Contrasts DHH's 'software as prose' with Uncle Bob's 'software as engineering discipline', framing the two modern AI development philosophies.
episodes.companion_video: DHH, Martin Fowler, Kent Beck: Is TDD Dead? (2014 Series)

episodes.title: Reputation & Proof of Work: Coderwall, Open Badges & Assembly
episodes.sound_above_inquiry: Who inspired the early efforts to measure developer reputation through open-source contributions rather than corporate pedigree?
episodes.chicago_context: Matt Deiters was an active Chicago Rubyist and startup founder exploring decentralized software work before web3 existed.
episodes.ai_era_parallel: When AI can generate any resume or fake code portfolio, cryptographic provenance and deterministic work histories are the only truth.

episodes.title: The Living Document: The Rise and Decline of Print Tech Books
episodes.sound_above_inquiry: Who inspired technical authors in the 1990s? How did the transition from physical book publishing to web hypertext alter developer learning?
episodes.chicago_context: WebVisions Chicago brought designers, authors, and front-end pioneers into conversation with system developers.
episodes.ai_era_parallel: Technical documentation has shifted from books to web to LLM context windows; preserving canonical provenance is more vital than ever.

episodes.title: Principles & Simplicity: Inventing on Principle & Simple Made Easy
episodes.sound_above_inquiry: What inspired Bret Victor and Rich Hickey to deliver the two most influential philosophical lectures of the modern software era?
episodes.chicago_context: Both talks deeply circulated through SCMC and Chicago dev meetups, becoming mandatory viewing for craftsmanship practitioners.
episodes.ai_era_parallel: Rich Hickey's separation of 'simple' (untangled) from 'easy' (familiar) is the definitive warning against complex AI framework sprawl.
episodes.companion_video: Bret Victor: Inventing on Principle (2012) & Rich Hickey: Simple Made Easy (2011)

episodes.era_name: The AI Horizon & The Observable Control Plane (2026)
episodes.title: Without zdots, There Was Nothing: Craftsmanship for Multi-Agent Fleets
episodes.sound_above_inquiry: What was the seventeen-year platform journey from Signatory #106 to local AI orchestration? Why does the machine have to be legible before agents arrive?
episodes.chicago_context: Mike Hall returns to SCMC in 2026 to present the local control plane, OpenTelemetry Jaeger traces, and sovereign inference.
episodes.ai_era_parallel: Language models are not magicians; they are fast autocompletes that require deterministic contracts, TDD verification, and strict boundaries.

episodes.era_name: The AI Horizon & The Observable Control Plane (2026)
episodes.title: The Sound Above Roundtable: What We Carry Forward
episodes.sound_above_inquiry: What is the sound above for the next generation of engineers? How do we build bridges rather than gates?
episodes.chicago_context: Bringing together veterans from Alt.NET, ChicagoRuby, 8th Light, Obtiva, and SCMC alongside new engineers entering tech today.
episodes.ai_era_parallel: Passing the flame of craftsmanship: human empathy, professional ethics, and architectural clarity in an AI-dominated industry.
